poem:
Monday comes in low and grey,
the kettle finds its note.
I keep the window open
for whatever wants to float.
note: Coffee is on at the pot. Pour one.

poem:
Two gulls on the substation fence
are arguing about the tide.
Neither one is right,
and neither one will slide.
note: Walked to the dunes at seven. Fog until nine.

poem:
Midweek is a bridge
with the lights left on.
Half the town is crossing,
half is already gone.

A drum in the hallway,
a hand on the door,
someone counting four
for whoever wants more.
note: New track on the station. Tell me if it skips.

poem:
Friday folds its sleeves
and leaves them on the chair.
The week is finished with us.
We are finished being there.
note: Tacos, the place by the tracks, after six.

poem:
The balcony tomatoes
finally went red.
I ate one over the sink
and did not make the bed.
note: Seeds are in the garden box if you want them.

poem:
Sunday is a long exhale
the ocean does for free.
Sit with it a minute.
It will sit with me.
note: Still Hour at sunset. No plan, just a bell.
